solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skilful when holding a knife

indicators.note: holding means the first word clasps the letter inside itself

parts.note: skilful means clever

explanation.surface: Someone deft at handling a blade while gripping a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's chopper with a broad heavy blade is a type of knife.

clue.text: Skip the whisky, it's child's play

parts.note: to skip is to hop
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: Advice to give the drink a miss because something is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: this is a playground game, not 'something easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground game of jumping through chalked squares is literally play for children.

clue.text: Mount rotates, showing no energy for stationary part

indicators.note: showing no signals that a letter is dropped from the reversed word
in a down clue, to mount is to climb, so the word rotates is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Engineering talk about a part that never turns, contrasted with one that rotates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' turns ROTATES into SETATOR; 'showing no energy' drops its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: In a motor or generator the fixed housing around the rotor is the non-moving component.

clue.text: Aircraft making journey by road!

parts.note: a trip is a journey
a lane is a small road

explanation.surface: An aeroplane that somehow gets about by road.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-winged aeroplane, as flown in the First World War, is an aircraft.

clue.text: 11.59 am greeting?

parts.note: one minute to noon is the very peak or end of the forenoon, so a greeting said then is literally at that point

explanation.surface: A greeting offered at one minute before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish-flavoured salutation is read literally: 11.59 is the uppermost point of the forenoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery, stereotypically Irish good-day salutation, taken literally as the last minute before noon.

clue.text: Essential to redraw triangle

indicators.note: to redraw a figure is to set it out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Geometry instructions insisting the shape must be drawn again.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral to a whole is fundamental and necessary to it, so essential.

clue.text: Hungarian composer of memorable harmonies

indicators.note: of signals the name is taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: Praise for a Hungarian composer whose harmonies stick in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar, the operetta composer of The Merry Widow, was born in Hungary.

clue.text: See rich now in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the letters again

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch wealthy people at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's see; 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Anglian city is the seat of an Anglican diocese, a bishop's see.

clue.text: Using maximum effort, tenth wicket has been taken

definitions.meaning: going flat out, holding nothing back
in cricket, when the tenth wicket falls the batting side's innings is over

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a team has eleven batsmen, so the fall of the tenth wicket ends the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Means total effort, and in cricket describes a batting side with no batsmen left.

clue.text: Stop to mend the lady's old penny crock

indicators.note: mending puts the broken word back together in a new order

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning the lady's
D stood for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A request to repair the woman's antique cheap pot.
explanation.walkthrough: D, from the Latin denarius, was the old British penny before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken fragment of earthenware can be called a crock, as in crocks in a flowerpot.

clue.text: Raised voice in argument beside river in Cornwall

indicators.note: beside places one piece next to the other

parts.note: the Fal is a river flowing into Falmouth in Cornwall
a set-to is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: Someone shouting during a row by a Cornish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised voice' suggests shouting, but it means a high-pitched singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing voice pitched above the natural range, used by male singers, is a raised register.

clue.text: Danger: Bill keeps caged rodent

indicators.note: keeps means the words hold the creature inside them

explanation.surface: A warning that someone called Bill keeps a pet in a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing desert rodent often kept as a pet in a cage.

clue.text: Circuit avoided by motorcade upset politician

indicators.note: upset means the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
avoided by means the letter is left out of the word that follows

parts.note: a circuit is a ring, shown by the round letter O

explanation.surface: A politician's motorcade swerves to skip a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from MOTORCADE leaves MTORCADE, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Democratic Party is a political figure.

clue.text: Problem — top teacher's a revolutionary

parts.note: the top teacher in a school is the head
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Trouble at school: the head turns out to be a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is figuratively a troublesome matter or worry.

clue.text: Shy relative

parts.note: a shy here is a throwing game, and the figure thrown at bears a kinship title and a woman's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid, but it is a fairground throwing game; the target figure is called after a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground figure that people throw things at, and so anyone made a target of criticism.

clue.text: Kind of circular that's run out covering United Nations course

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering puts the first pieces on top of the next

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is short for out in cricket scoring
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A leaflet about a run-out that wraps a UN course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a leaflet but means round in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approximately round in shape is a sort of circular.

clue.text: Sloppy sentimentality has space to grow quickly

parts.note: mush is soppy sentimental stuff
room is space

explanation.surface: Gushing sentiment that has room to expand fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand or spread rapidly, like fungi springing up overnight.

clue.text: Discover a foreign planet

parts.note: un is the French for a, so a foreign a
Earth is a planet

explanation.surface: Finding an alien world.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up or bring to light, hence to find out something.

clue.text: Wild flower's name included

indicators.note: included means the letter is placed within the flower

parts.note: a violet is a flower

explanation.surface: A wild flower's name is put on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild flower' reads as one phrase, but 'Wild' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild and violent both describe something unrestrained and fierce, as in a storm.

clue.text: In the open air, take clothes off — that's better

parts.note: out means outdoors
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: Undressing outdoors and finding it an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective but is a verb: to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip a rival is to exceed or surpass them, to do better.

clue.text: Jack provided fellow's price list

parts.note: a jack or tar is a sailor
if means provided that
F is short for fellow

explanation.surface: A sailor's conditional reference to a man's catalogue of charges.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack tar and tar are both old names for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of charges or rates, a list of prices.

clue.text: One churchman or another going round Colorado

indicators.note: going round means the second churchman surrounds the state abbreviation

parts.note: another churchman is a dean, head of a cathedral chapter
CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado

explanation.surface: Two clergymen, one encircling a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister below a priest, so a churchman.

clue.text: Old town lake and waterway

parts.note: Cana is the ancient Galilean town of the wedding miracle
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An ancient settlement with a lake and a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial channel for boats, a waterway.

clue.text: Man casually meeting friend as a rule

parts.note: Norm is the casual short form of the name Norman
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A man casually bumping into a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' does not shorten anything itself here: it says to use a man's name in its informal form.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means usually, in the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: Migrating bird is in Italian port

indicators.note: migrating means moving about, so these letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: A migrant bird turns up in a harbour in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a port on the Adriatic coast of southern Italy.

clue.text: Cat not in life nine, frisky

indicators.note: frisky means lively, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cat, not in its ninth life, still lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' says the letters of IN are removed from LIFE NINE before the leftover letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline is used as a noun for any member of the cat family.

clue.text: The lengths a complete swine will go to?

definitions.text: The lengths a complete swine will go to?

parts.words: The lengths a complete swine will go to?
parts.note: an entire pig is a full porker, and going all the way is to go the full distance

explanation.surface: Wondering how far a total rotter will stoop.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'go the whole ...' means do something thoroughly; read literally it is an entire pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doing something completely, without half measures, read as a whole pig.
